subject: FinEdge — SLA uplift & latency carve-out request
messages:
From: Amelia Stone <amelia.stone@finedge.io>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Hale <marcus.hale@finedge.io>, FinEdge Procurement <procurement@finedge.io>
Date: Tue, 05 Jan 2027 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: SLA ask — uptime threshold + low-latency carve-out

Thanks for the demo last week — FinEdge team is keen to move forward, but procurement flagged two items in Redwood's standard SLA that we'd like to discuss before redlining:

1) Uptime guarantee: the standard 99.9% uptime is great, but for our primary trading workloads we need a firm 99.95% target for the two high-availability regions during market hours (06:00–18:00 ET).

2) Latency: some of our calls are ultra-low-latency (<=25ms p99). We understand global rolling maintenance and bursting are part of the product; procurement wants a carve-out where latency SLOs are defined separately and a limited exception to the standard credit table if we experience latency regressions caused by model fallbacks.

Can Redwood provide a proposed amendment that shows:
- a regional uptime uplift during market hours,
- an explicit latency carve-out with measurable metrics and a smaller credit multiplier for transient fallbacks, and
- an agreed maintenance schedule etiquette (notification windows, emergency maintenance escalation)?

We can loop in legal and SRE next week. Attaching a short CSV with sample p95/p99 calls.

Thanks,
Amelia
Procurement Lead — FinEdge
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Stone <amelia.stone@finedge.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 05 Jan 2027 11:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SLA ask — uptime threshold + low-latency carve-out

Amelia — really appreciate the clear ask and the sample metrics. Quick responses to each point and next steps below.

High level proposal:
- Uptime: We can agree to a 99.95% regional uptime target for the two named regions during the specified market window, with a one-year pilot period tied to usage thresholds.
- Latency carve-out: We propose defining a separate latency SLO (p99 <= 30ms) for the "trading" route, with a smaller credit multiplier (0.5x) for transient model fallback events that meet our documented short-lived fallback definition (<= 5 minutes, automatically detected).
- Maintenance: Standard notification remains 72 hours for scheduled maintenance; for emergency maintenance impacting market hours we commit to an on-call escalation path and targeted rollback playbook.

We will draft a narrow SLA amendment that:
- enumerates market-hours window and regions,
- includes explicit metric definitions and measurement method (server-side p99, regional aggregation), and
- adjusts the credit bands for latency-driven credits for fallbacks vs. full-service interruptions.

Action items:
1) Ben & Rishi — can you draft the technical metric language and a short decision flow for what qualifies as a fallback vs. service interruption?
2) Laura — work with legal to craft the amendment template and flagged redlines around pilot duration and termination rights.
3) Amelia — share the list of region names and any regulatory constraints your security team needs us to include.

I'll follow up with a first-draft PDF by EOD Friday.

— Soojin
SoojIn Lee
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Amelia Stone <amelia.stone@finedge.io>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 06 Jan 2027 09:37:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SLA ask — uptime threshold + low-latency carve-out

Amelia, Soojin — adding the technical framing. Draft notes below that I'll fold into the amendment doc:

Measurement approach:
- Uptime: regional availability computed hourly; market-hours uptime is measured as the percentage of minutes without an availability-failing condition across the two regions during the 06:00–18:00 ET window.
- Latency SLO: route-level server-side p99 latency over a rolling 30-day window; data source is Redwood telemetry (customers may provide agent logs for reconciliation).

Fallback vs interruption:
- Fallback = automatic model variant switch with degraded latency but continued functionality; defined as: (a) rollback or fallback executed automatically, (b) end-to-end impact < 5 minutes per incident, (c) no data loss and no API 5xx spike beyond transient thresholds. Falls matching this are eligible for the reduced credit multiplier.
- Interruption = service unavailable or sustained degradation > 5 minutes, or API 5xx spike correlated with request failure; these follow the standard credit table.

Credit proposal (monthly):
- Uptime shortfall bands (market-hours regional):
  * 99.95–99.90% => 5% credit of monthly usage for impacted routes
  * 99.90–99.00% => 15% credit
  * <99.00% => 35% credit
- Latency fallback band:
  * If latency SLO missed due to a qualifying fallback => 2.5% credit (0.5x of the standard 5% band)
  * If latency missed due to sustained regression or rollout => standard latency credit bands apply (5–20% depending on severity).

I'll attach a sample amendment PDF and the raw latency CSV. We should be explicit about instrumentation and time-synchronization requirements for reconciliation.

— Ben
Principal Sales Engineer
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Stone <amelia.stone@finedge.io>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 08 Jan 2027 15:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SLA ask — uptime threshold + low-latency carve-out

Team — finalizing the narrow amendment for your review. Summary of what's in the attached draft SLA_Amendment_FE-879_draft.pdf:

- Market-hours regional uptime uplift: 99.95% target for Region-1 and Region-3 during 06:00–18:00 ET; 12-month pilot with quarterly review and objective usage > $50k/month to keep the uplift.
- Latency carve-out: a separate latency SLO for the route named "trading-write" (p99 <= 30ms). Qualifying fallbacks are explicitly defined and mapped to a 2.5% monthly credit band when invoked.
- Credit mechanics: credits are applied to monthly invoice; both parties can request reconciliation via telemetry export within 30 days of invoice.
- Maintenance & emergency ops: 72-hour scheduled notice; emergency ops require immediate notification and a post-incident report within 48 hours for any market-hours event.

Next steps for sign-off:
- Amelia — mark any legal redlines you need (we'll incorporate).
- Laura & Rishi — I'll send the PDF to Legal and SRE for final wording edits and instrumented metric definitions.
- If procurement confirms no further redlines, we'll route to DocuSign (link included in the email).

Amelia — appreciate the collaboration; happy to hop on a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk the amendment line by line if that helps.

Best,
SoojIn Lee
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
Attachments: SLA_Amendment_FE-879_draft.pdf, latency-sample-weekly.csv
